Click: tip out. Click: tip in. How does it remember?
Below it: the same parts, unrolled flat.
Fixed in the barrel. Their slopes end in a pocket or a gap, taking turns.
Its bottom edge is a ring of slanted saw teeth.
Carries the ink refill. The spring pushes it up. Follow the red lug.
The button pushes the cam down, below the ribs.
The slanted teeth push the lug half a step sideways.
The spring pushes the cam up. The rib slope slides it the other half step.
The lug stops in the pocket and stays down. Tip out.
The teeth: half a step again.
The slope: the other half. Now the lug is under a gap...
...so the spring pushes it all the way up. Tip in.
Every click turns the cam 1/8 of a turn.
Press + release: the lug stops in a pocket.
Next click it rises up a gap. That's the whole trick.
